questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Source Documents and Accounting Vouchers' refers to.
questions.a: Written proofs of financial exchanges such as cash memos and bills serve as source documents, from which formal accounting vouchers are prepared to authorize debit and credit entries.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Source Documents and Accounting Vouchers'.
questions.a: Every business entry must be supported by verifiable documentary evidence arranged chronologically.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Source Documents and Accounting Vouchers' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 3.1 (source: keac103.txt lines 25-80)

questions.q: Find total assets when liabilities and capital are given. Use the method 'Fundamental Accounting Equation'. Work with: capital = 5000, liabilities = 120. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of assets.
questions.a: 5120 rupees

questions.q: Calculate total resources of the firm. Use the method 'Fundamental Accounting Equation'. Work with: capital = 5000, liabilities = 4. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of assets.
questions.a: 5004 rupees

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Fundamental Accounting Equation' refers to.
questions.a: A mathematical statement demonstrating that total economic resources owned by an entity always equal the sum of claims held by external lenders and internal owners.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Fundamental Accounting Equation'.
questions.a: Dual-aspect accounting ensures the equality of resources and financing claims at all points in time.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Fundamental Accounting Equation', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: assets = liabilities + capital

concepts.title: Derivation of Capital or Liabilities from Accounting Equation

questions.q: Calculate capital when assets are ... and liabilities are .... Use the method 'Derivation of Capital or Liabilities from Accounting Equation'. Work with: assets = 500, liabilities = 300. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of capital.
questions.a: 200 rupees

questions.q: Find outsider liabilities if assets and capital are known. Use the method 'Derivation of Capital or Liabilities from Accounting Equation'. Work with: assets = 2500, liabilities = 3. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of capital.
questions.a: 2497 rupees

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Derivation of Capital or Liabilities from Accounting Equation' refers to.
questions.a: Calculating an unknown component of the balance sheet equation by isolating either capital or liabilities from total assets.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Derivation of Capital or Liabilities from Accounting Equation'.
questions.a: Owner's residual equity equals total assets less outsider claims.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Derivation of Capital or Liabilities from Accounting Equation', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: capital = assets - liabilities

concepts.title: Adjustment to Capital for Profit, Drawings, and Additional Investment

questions.q: Calculate closing capital at the end of the year. Use the method 'Adjustment to Capital for Profit, Drawings, and Additional Investment'. Work with: drawings = 12, expenses = 5000, fresh_capital = 2500, opening_capital = 8000, revenue = 8000. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of closing_capital.
questions.a: 13488 rupees

questions.q: Find the updated capital after revenue expenses and drawings. Use the method 'Adjustment to Capital for Profit, Drawings, and Additional Investment'. Work with: drawings = 200, expenses = 500, fresh_capital = 500, opening_capital = 1200, revenue = 5000. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of closing_capital.
questions.a: 6000 rupees

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Adjustment to Capital for Profit, Drawings, and Additional Investment' refers to.
questions.a: Closing capital is derived by adjusting beginning capital with operational revenues, business expenses, fresh funds invested, and withdrawals made by the proprietor.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Adjustment to Capital for Profit, Drawings, and Additional Investment'.
questions.a: Revenues and fresh capital expand equity, whereas expenses and drawings diminish it.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Adjustment to Capital for Profit, Drawings, and Additional Investment', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: closing_capital = opening_capital + fresh_capital + revenue - expenses - drawings

concepts.title: Modern Rules of Debit and Credit

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Modern Rules of Debit and Credit' refers to.
questions.a: The system governing account entries: assets and expenses increase by debit and decrease by credit, whereas liabilities, capital, and revenues increase by credit and decrease by debit.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Modern Rules of Debit and Credit'.
questions.a: Debits increase asset and expense balances; credits increase liability, capital, and revenue balances.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Modern Rules of Debit and Credit' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 3.3.1 (source: keac103.txt lines 195-265)

concepts.title: Journalising Transactions in the Book of Original Entry

questions.q: Using the method 'Journalising Transactions in the Book of Original Entry', work with: total_credit = 200. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of total_debit.
questions.a: 200 units

questions.q: Take the relation taught for 'Journalising Transactions in the Book of Original Entry' and work with: total_credit = 50. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of total_debit.
questions.a: 50 units

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Journalising Transactions in the Book of Original Entry' refers to.
questions.a: Recording financial events chronologically in a five-column journal format specifying debited accounts, credited accounts, amounts, and explanatory narrations.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Journalising Transactions in the Book of Original Entry'.
questions.a: Every journal entry preserves the dual-aspect equality by having identical aggregate debit and credit sums.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Journalising Transactions in the Book of Original Entry', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: total_debit = total_credit

questions.q: Calculate CGST and SGST on goods purchased for .... Use the method 'Intra-State and Inter-State GST Computation'. Work with: base_amount = 2500, cgst_rate = 5, sgst_rate = 25. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of invoice_total.
questions.a: 3250 units

questions.q: Compute the total invoice amount including GST. Use the method 'Intra-State and Inter-State GST Computation'. Work with: base_amount = 120000, cgst_rate = 10, sgst_rate = 20. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of invoice_total.
questions.a: 156000 units

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Intra-State and Inter-State GST Computation' refers to.
questions.a: Computing Goods and Services Tax wherein intra-state supplies are taxed equally as Central GST and State GST, while inter-state supplies are subject to Integrated GST.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Intra-State and Inter-State GST Computation'.
questions.a: Intra-state purchases split GST equally between CGST and SGST, whereas inter-state trade levies full IGST.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Intra-State and Inter-State GST Computation', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: cgst = base_amount * cgst_rate / 100; sgst = base_amount * sgst_rate / 100; invoice_total = base_amount + cgst + sgst

concepts.title: Net GST Settlement through Input Tax Credit

questions.q: Calculate the net GST payable to the government. Use the method 'Net GST Settlement through Input Tax Credit'. Work with: input_tax = 20, output_tax = 18. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of net_tax_payable.
questions.a: -2 rupees

questions.q: How much net tax is paid through electronic cash ledger? Use the method 'Net GST Settlement through Input Tax Credit'. Work with: input_tax = 20, output_tax = 20. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of net_tax_payable.
questions.a: 0 rupees

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Net GST Settlement through Input Tax Credit' refers to.
questions.a: Offsetting the input tax credit paid on procurement against output tax collected from customers to compute the net tax payable to the government.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Net GST Settlement through Input Tax Credit'.
questions.a: The government receives only the value-addition tax, computed as output tax minus eligible input tax credit.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Net GST Settlement through Input Tax Credit', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: net_tax_payable = output_tax - input_tax

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Ledger Accounts and Posting Mechanism' refers to.
questions.a: Transferring debits and credits recorded in chronological journal entries to individual analytical ledger accounts to summarize balances.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Ledger Accounts and Posting Mechanism'.
questions.a: Posting organizes transactions by individual accounts in the principal book to determine balances at any given time.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Ledger Accounts and Posting Mechanism' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 3.5 (source: keac103.txt lines 625-720)

concepts.title: Apportionment of Insolvent Debt into Recovery and Bad Debts

questions.q: Calculate bad debts when a debtor pays ... paise in a rupee. Use the method 'Apportionment of Insolvent Debt into Recovery and Bad Debts'. Work with: recovery_rate = 15, total_debt = 24. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of bad_debts.
questions.a: 20.4 rupees

questions.q: Find the cash recovered and amount written off as bad debt. Use the method 'Apportionment of Insolvent Debt into Recovery and Bad Debts'. Work with: recovery_rate = 25, total_debt = 80. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of bad_debts.
questions.a: 60 rupees

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Apportionment of Insolvent Debt into Recovery and Bad Debts' refers to.
questions.a: Calculating the portion of debt recovered in cash versus the irrecoverable loss written off as bad debts when a debtor is declared insolvent.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Apportionment of Insolvent Debt into Recovery and Bad Debts'.
questions.a: Dividend from an insolvent debtor's estate is debited to cash/bank and the remaining deficit to bad debts account.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Apportionment of Insolvent Debt into Recovery and Bad Debts', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: recovered_amount = total_debt * recovery_rate / 100; bad_debts = total_debt - recovered_amount

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Computation of Interest on Capital' refers to.
questions.a: Determining the interest allowable to the proprietor on capital invested in the business for a specific time period at a stated annual percentage rate.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Computation of Interest on Capital'.
questions.a: Interest on capital is treated as a business expense and increases the owner's total capital claim.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Computation of Interest on Capital', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: interest = capital * rate * months / 1200
